answer:
**Best estimate:** **10,200,000 units** of **Coca-Cola** sold in the **CSD/sodavand category in Danish retail in January 2026**.

**Estimated range:** **7,500,000–14,000,000 units**  
**Confidence:** **Low-to-moderate, ~45%** — mainly because brand-level monthly retail unit sales are not public, and “unit” can vary by data provider. I’m treating a unit as an individual retail consumer container/pack equivalent, not liters or DKK.

**How I estimated it:**

- Danish sources indicate high soft-drink consumption: about **82 liters of sodavand per person per year**, with total sweet-drink purchases around **127 liters per person** in the cited FVST/DTU material. ([foedevarestyrelsen.dk](https://foedevarestyrelsen.dk/Media/638763454077872158/5%20h%C3%A5ndfulde_faktaark.pdf))  
- DTU cites Euromonitor-based 2025 Danish soft-drink sales of **966 million liters**, and notes that soda/CSD retail/off-trade is the relevant channel for brand shares. ([food.dtu.dk](https://www.food.dtu.dk/english/-/media/institutter/foedevareinstituttet/publikationer/pub-2025/markeds-og-vareundersoegelse-af-energidrikke-i-danmark-final-report.pdf))  
- Euromonitor’s Denmark carbonates summary says 2025 retail volume declined significantly, partly from weaker cola demand and anti-US sentiment affecting Coca-Cola, so I applied a haircut to Coca-Cola’s share versus a normal year. ([marketresearch.com](https://www.marketresearch.com/Euromonitor-International-v746/Carbonates-Denmark-43236730/?utm_source=openai))  
- I assumed roughly **470–490 million liters/year** of Danish retail CSD, **~22% Coca-Cola brand share**, **~6.7% of annual sales occurring in January**, and **~0.70 L per sold unit** on average across cans, 0.5L bottles, and larger PET bottles. Coca-Cola Denmark’s listed formats span **0.25L, 0.33L, 0.5L, 1L, 1.25L, 1.5L, 1.75L and 2L**, supporting the need for a weighted average pack size assumption. ([carlsbergdanmark.dk](https://www.carlsbergdanmark.dk/produkter/coca-cola/coca-cola/?Ckey=12497&utm_source=openai))
